problem: A PreToolUse hook (tool-call guard) that maps each file write to a project record took the project root from the harness's project directory (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) before anything else. In a repository that contains more than one record (a monorepo, an examples directory, a nested example app with its own .eccode/), every write into the nested project was judged by the OUTER record (wrong root): the nested project's reviewers were denied their own draft area, its authors were denied their own artifacts directory, and its implementers were checked against the outer record's task claims instead of their own. Dispatches fail even though the agent did exactly what its role allows.
symptoms: PreToolUse hook denies a reviewer's Write to <nested>/.eccode/reviews/drafts/...: "architecture-reviewer reviews/designs but does not edit project files; write drafts under .eccode/artifacts/ or .eccode/reviews/drafts/." (the message contains no path)
Author role (product-architect) denied every Write under <nested>/.eccode/artifacts/ although that is its draft area
draft area denied only in a nested project (examples/<app>/, monorepo package); the same role in a top-level project is allowed

the denied target lies inside the role's own draft or artifact area of the NESTED record (examples/<app>/.eccode/reviews/drafts/..., examples/<app>/.eccode/artifacts/..., examples/<app>/.eccode/drafts/...)

implementer holding a claimed task in the NESTED record is denied with "<role> has no claimed task. Claim one first ..." or "<path relative to the outer repository, e.g. examples/<app>/src/x.js> is outside the ownership of <role>'s claimed task(s): <the OUTER record's claims>", because the guard read the outer record's tasks (by code reading of a088c6a checkEdit: `state = new Store(root).state()` with root = outer; not exercised by the reproduction check)
agent falls back to writing its review from a scratch path, or asks the orchestrator to copy files in

steps: Check script: node .eccode/drafts/nested-root-check.js <guard.js>. It runs the GUARD FILE GIVEN AS ARGUMENT (not scripts/hooks/guard.js) and first prints that file's path and sha256, so the evidence log pins the file under test (the record's tree digest excludes .eccode/). It builds a throwaway git repo with an outer record and a nested examples/app record (lib/project init), then pipes two PreToolUse payloads to that guard with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<outer> and cwd=<outer>, agent_type eccode:architecture-reviewer: (a) Write examples/app/.eccode/reviews/drafts/architecture-1.json must be allowed; (b) Write examples/app/.eccode/state.json must be denied. Exit 0 if both are right, 1 if the guard misjudges, 2 on harness error.

Reproduction: .eccode/drafts/guard-under-test.js = copy of scripts/hooks/guard.js at commit a088c6a (pre-repair; sha256 25bb07dcc39984c5f8ebef7b278f1ed62dd0f6a19133270572bd93ac5f669289, equal to `git show a088c6a:scripts/hooks/guard.js`), command: node .eccode/drafts/nested-root-check.js .eccode/drafts/guard-under-test.js -> exit 1; nestedDraftWrite 'denied (wrong)' with the pilot's exact message; nestedRecordWrite 'denied (correct)'. Pinned run: ev:ev-mv1b0cid-0189968e (prints the sha256); first run without the sha256 line: ev:ev-mv1aqo8u-01378a06.

Verification: the same file replaced by a copy of the current scripts/hooks/guard.js (HEAD ad69e6d, file last changed in 1fcda26; sha256 d43f4b548e86029a311b969b560fa84e56ac30aac598ff9faf234bf2d279c630, equal to `git show HEAD:scripts/hooks/guard.js`), identical command -> exit 0.

Caveat: both guard copies load lib/ two directories up, i.e. the CURRENT engine (HEAD ad69e6d), not a088c6a's lib/. The functions the guard uses exist in both versions; the only variable between the failing and the passing run is the guard file itself.
The check exercises the reviewer role only; the implementer symptom (claims read from the outer record) follows from the a088c6a code and is not reproduced here.

Original occurrence: RescueStock pilot (examples/rescuestock/.eccode), runs run-mv16bo0q (architecture-reviewer, Write to .eccode/reviews/drafts/ denied) and run-mv16pz5f (product-architect, every Write under .eccode/artifacts/ denied); examples/rescuestock/docs/pilot-report.md.

rootCause.explanation: Pre-repair guard (commit a088c6a, scripts/hooks/guard.js): L453 `const root = findRoot(process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || input.cwd || process.cwd());` then, for Edit/Write, L463-464 `const abs = path.resolve(input.cwd || root, target); const rel = toPosix(path.relative(root, abs));`. findRoot was lexical: `if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, '.eccode', 'events.jsonl'))) return dir;`. The harness sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to the outer repository, so root = outer and rel = 'examples/app/.eccode/reviews/drafts/architecture-1.json'. Role draft areas (draftAreas, L74-78) are matched relative to root ('.eccode/reviews/drafts/**', '.eccode/artifacts/**'), so the nested draft area matched nothing and checkEdit fell through to L446 `out('deny', `${role} reviews/designs but does not edit project files; ...`)`, a message with no path. For implementer roles the same wrong root reaches the claim check: `state = new Store(root).state()` reads the OUTER record's tasks, so a claim held in the nested record is invisible ('has no claimed task') or the outer-relative path is tested against the outer claims ('is outside the ownership'). One root per hook call, taken from the harness, cannot be right for a target that lives under a different record. Repaired guard (merged in 0.3.1; file last changed in 1fcda26): (1) L640 the hook cwd is tried before the harness dir: `const root = findRoot(input.cwd || process.cwd()) || findRoot(process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd());`; (2) L659 every target picks its own root from its real path: `const abs = realize(lexical); ... const fileRoot = findRoot(path.dirname(abs)) || root; // the nearest record above the file decides` and `rel = path.relative(fileRoot, abs)`. Finding from this investigation: in the check (and in the pilot, where the orchestrator's cwd was the outer repo) the hook cwd IS the outer repository, so the cwd-before-CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR reordering alone changes nothing; the per-target root (2) is what fixes the pilot case. findRoot (L178) now walks real paths and accepts `<dir>/.eccode` only if it is a real directory and not a symbolic link (`!fs.lstatSync(rec).isSymbolicLink() && fs.statSync(rec).isDirectory()`), holds events.jsonl, and `dir` does not itself lie inside another record (`!insideRecord(dir)`). Record files are denied on both the lexical and the real path before any root is chosen (`recordHit(lexical)`), so a nested root can never turn a record into ordinary files. Evidence: the same check fails with the a088c6a guard copy (sha256 25bb07dc..., printed in the log) and passes with the current guard copy (sha256 d43f4b54..., printed in the log); the guard file is the only variable.

failedAttempts.approach: Review round 1 (commit ffbdc8d, the first nested-root repair): 'nearest .eccode wins', resolved lexically: walk up from the target and take the first directory with .eccode/events.jsonl.
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Independent review F2 (changes requested): a record planted inside the record (`mkdir -p .eccode/.eccode && cp -r ./.eccode/. .eccode/.eccode/`, or `init --root .eccode`) became the nearest root, so the outer record's own files were judged as that bogus project's ordinary files and the main session could write them. Lesson: a directory lying inside a record must never count as a root.

failedAttempts.approach: Review round 2 (80ddab0, reviewed at head d0e2a3b): record-directory regexes (RECORD_DIR_WRITE, introduced in 80ddab0) to refuse shell commands that copy or plant a record, keeping the lexical root search.
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Re-review G1/G8 (changes requested): bypassed by prefixed or quoted spellings (`cp -r ./.eccode/. "$PWD/.eccode/.eccode"`; the regex wanted the bare word `.eccode`) and by an alias `ln -s "$PWD/.eccode" rec`: findRoot saw rec/.eccode/events.jsonl through the link, rec became the root, and `Write rec/state.json` was allowed. Patterns over command text cannot enumerate spellings; this led to the structural rewrite on real paths.

failedAttempts.approach: Review round 3 (3fa6298): structural rewrite: realize() every target, everything under a record except the draft areas is the record, real-path findRoot that rejects links and records inside records.
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Re-review H1/H2 (changes requested): a link created and written through in the SAME command line (`ln -s "$PWD/.eccode" lk && echo FORGED > lk/state.json`) was allowed, because lk does not exist when the guard runs and realize() fell back to the lexical path; bash clobbered the real state.json (1995 -> 7 bytes). H2: the same through a dangling link that already exists from an earlier turn. Closed in 9c4d5aa (review round 4: approve, with the non-blocking over-denial I1): dangling links followed by hand, and a line that creates a link and writes is refused.

failedAttempts.approach: Review round 5 (beb7fbb): narrowing the round-4 'line creates a link and writes' rule to fire only when a link operand textually names a record (mentionsRecord) or is computed, to stop over-denying record-free build lines (finding I1).
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Re-review J1 (changes requested): a two-turn chained alias defeats it. Turn 1 `ln -s "$PWD/.eccode" a` (single target, allowed); turn 2 `ln -s a b && echo FORGED > b/state.json` names no record, b does not exist yet so realize() falls back to the lexical path, and bash clobbered the real state.json (1995 -> 7 bytes). Closed in 1fcda26 (approved): a link operand that resolves through existing links into a record counts as a record operand.

verification.regressionTest: node --test tests/guard-verification-repairs.test.js tests/review-F4-F5-guard.test.js tests/hooks-install.test.js (30/30 pass, ev:ev-mv1ar25z-01bc1bdf). Nested case: tests/guard-verification-repairs.test.js 'NESTED: a project nested in a repository with its own record is judged by its own record'. Failed attempts covered by 'REVIEW: a record planted inside a record never re-roots the guard; the record directory itself is the CLI's', 'REVIEW 2: targets are judged on their real path for everyone: aliases, spellings, directory operations, pipes', 'REVIEW 3: a link created and written through in one line, and a dangling link that already exists, cannot reach the record'. Verification runs: the reproduction command, identical, with .eccode/drafts/guard-under-test.js replaced by a copy of the current scripts/hooks/guard.js (HEAD ad69e6d, file last changed in 1fcda26) -> exit 0, nested draft allowed, nested record denied; ev:ev-mv1b0exx-018a8c87 prints sha256 d43f4b54... of the file under test.

appliesWhen: any hook or guard (PreToolUse hook, pre-commit hook, policy check) that maps file writes to a project record or project root, in a repository that contains more than one record
monorepos where packages or services carry their own project record or config directory
example apps or pilots nested under examples/ in a toolkit repository that has its own .eccode/

a role is denied a write whose target lies inside its own draft or artifact area of the NESTED record (examples/<app>/.eccode/reviews/drafts, .../artifacts, .../drafts), while the same write is allowed in a top-level project
an implementer that holds a claimed task in the NESTED record is denied with 'has no claimed task' or 'is outside the ownership of ... claimed task(s)' listing the outer record's claims (or none)
designing root discovery that must resist symlink aliases or a record copied inside a record (wrong root, re-rooting)
notApplicableWhen: a reviewer or designer was denied for a target that lies OUTSIDE its draft and artifact areas of the record that owns the target (e.g. it edited examples/<app>/src/... in the correct project): that is the role rule working, not a wrong root

a claim denial ('has no claimed task' / 'outside the ownership') when the nested record holds no matching claim either, or when the listed claims are the target project's own: claim the task or report the need to the orchestrator
harnesses that do not pass cwd or a project directory to the hook, or hooks that receive no file path: root resolution there is a different problem
single-record repositories: the harness project directory and the target's nearest record coincide
the eccode CLI itself writing to the wrong record (e.g. `eccode init` without --root walking up to the outer record): same family of symptom, different component; pass --root explicitly

a Bash heredoc or inline program refused because its TEXT names a record path ('ECCode project record files are written only by the eccode CLI'): that is the raw-text over-denial, not a wrong root; write drafts with the Write tool
a record file write denied in a nested project: record files are written only by the CLI everywhere; this is correct behaviour
